questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, an object covers 60 m in 20 seconds along a straight line from the origin. What is the object's speed?
questions.explanation: The gradient of a distance-time graph equals the speed. Gradient = change in distance / change in time = 60/20 = 3 m/s. Option (a) calculates time/distance instead of distance/time. Option (d) multiplies distance by time. Always remember: on a distance-time graph, gradient = speed.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line represent?

options.text: The object is moving at constant speed

questions.explanation: A horizontal line on a distance-time graph means the distance is not changing over time — the object is stationary. The gradient is zero, meaning speed = 0. Option (a) would be shown by a straight diagonal line. Option (b) would appear as a curve getting steeper.

questions.stem: Two objects are shown on the same distance-time graph. Object A has a steeper straight line than Object B. What can you conclude?

options.text: Object A has travelled a greater distance
Object A is moving at a greater constant speed
Object A is accelerating while Object B is not

questions.explanation: On a distance-time graph, the gradient equals speed. A steeper straight line means a larger gradient, which means greater speed. Both lines are straight, so both objects move at constant speed (not accelerating). The steepness tells us about speed, not about total distance or start time.

questions.stem: A distance-time graph shows a curve that gets progressively steeper over time. What type of motion does this represent?

options.text: The object is stationary then starts moving

questions.explanation: A curve getting steeper means the gradient is increasing over time. Since gradient = speed on a distance-time graph, increasing gradient means increasing speed, which is acceleration. A curve getting less steep would indicate deceleration. A straight line would indicate constant speed.

questions.stem: A student walks to school. For the first 200 seconds, the distance-time graph shows a straight line reaching 400 m. The student then waits at a crossing for 100 seconds. What is the average speed for the entire 300 seconds?
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = 400 / 300 = 1.33 m/s. Option (b) uses only the walking time (400/200 = 2 m/s), which gives the speed during the walking phase only. The stationary period must be included in the total time for average speed, even though no distance was covered.
